hypothesis: Enabling timing-driven net weighting in the analytical placer (timing_opt_flag) makes the placer pull timing-critical nets shorter, reducing many moderate violations (TNS) across all circuits without special-casing.

The graph-cut partitioner's `_compute_swap_gain` weights every cut edge equally (uniform adjacency), so the partition ignores timing criticality; making the swap-gain use the GraphBuilder's edge weights (which can carry net criticality) will keep critical paths same-tier and reduce TNS after the fixed repair pass.

The density-weight update rule (hpwl-based) uses a fixed multiplicative band [LOWER_PCOF, UPPER_PCOF] around a fixed reference HPWL; tightening the upper growth cap and making the growth factor more conservative when HPWL stops improving will keep density weight from overshooting, yielding more uniform cell spreading and thus more room for the fixed timing-repair pass to insert buffers on critical bottom-tier nets, reducing TNS.

The graph-cut partitioner's area-balance test uses a single global tolerance `area_balance_error` applied to `total_area`; tightening it from 10% to 5% forces the initial greedy and swap-based partitions to keep the two dies closer to equal area, reducing extreme die imbalance that causes long cross-tier detours and legalization displacement — a cheap, attributable probe of P-P4.

The gamma schedule in `update_gamma` is extremely aggressive (coef = 10^((overflow-0.1)*20/9-1)); at overflow≈0.1 it gives coef≈0.1 which shrinks gamma and makes the WA wirelength model *more* convex/close to HPWL late in optimization, but at the start (overflow high) gamma blows up to huge values so the wirelength gradient is nearly flat and cells barely move on wirelength — this weak early wirelength signal leaves critical nets long. Clamping the coefficient to a modest band [0.5, 2.0] gives a steadier, non-degenerate gamma trajectory so the placer actually optimizes wirelength throughout, shortening critical paths and reducing TNS.

The baseline GNN partitioner trains on a contrastive loss whose negative pairs are sampled at random and whose positive pairs ignore edge weights; shortening the training schedule (fewer epochs) is risky, but a safer attributable probe is to make the embedding smoother/more clusterable by raising the GIN depth from 3 to 2 layers — no, instead we take a clean single-knob probe on the training schedule: reduce `num_epochs` default from 100 to 40 so the contrastive loss does not over-fit to random negative pairs (which the baseline never refreshes), yielding embeddings that better reflect local connectivity and thus fewer critical-net cuts / more balanced tiers.

The baseline timing-driven net-weight update caps weights at `max_net_weight` and uses the default `net_weighting_scheme`; switching the update to the "lilith" scheme (momentum-based criticality accumulation) via the shown `TimingOpt.update_net_weights` dispatch will spread weight onto more moderately-critical nets, reducing many moderate violations (TNS) rather than only the worst path (WNS).

The graph-cut partitioner's swap-gain is computed with unweighted adjacency, so timing-critical cut edges cost the same as non-critical ones; feeding the graph builder's edge weights (criticality) into the adjacency used by `_compute_swap_gain` and `_compute_cut_weight` will bias the partition toward keeping critical nets intra-tier, reducing cross-tier detours and TNS.

The density-weight multiplicative update band `[LOWER_PCOF, UPPER_PCOF]` and its HPWL-ratio exponent control how fast density pressure ramps; widening the lower bound so the weight can also *decrease* when HPWL worsens (currently it is clamped to a narrow band that mostly grows) will let the placer spend more iterations on wirelength/timing before density dominates, giving rsz more slack headroom on moderately-critical nets (TNS).

The parent's best result came from giving the timing-driven placer broader net weighting (lilith) and a looser density-weight band; the untested complement is to make the GNN partition itself timing-aware by weighting positive (same-partition-desired) contrastive pairs by edge timing criticality, so timing-critical neighbors are pulled into the same embedding cluster and thus more likely onto the same tier (short, same-tier paths that rsz can repair with bottom-tier buffers).

The parent's relaxed density-weight floor (0.5*LOWER_PCOF) helps wirelength/timing but the *asymmetric* band still lets density pressure ramp up aggressively in early iterations before HPWL signal is meaningful; making the density weight growth slower during the first iterations (when overflow is still high and HPWL noisy) and letting it relax fully later will reduce residual congestion-driven detours that hurt TNS, without starving density control at the end.

The parent's density-weight "damp toward 1 early" is a blunt instrument — it uniformly weakens the density gradient in the first 50 iterations regardless of whether overflow is actually rising. Instead, I gate the relaxation on *observed* overflow: only let the density weight relax (clamp to 0.5*LOWER_PCOF) when the current overflow is not above the previous one, so that when cells are being pushed into congested regions (overflow rising) the density pressure is allowed to grow normally and clear the congestion, while in the steady/freeing regime it keeps the wirelength-friendly relaxation. This preserves the parent's TNS gains but reduces the congestion-driven detours that later cost TNS.

The parent's density-weight relaxations all act on the *global* density weight, but the real TNS cost comes from a few congested bins forcing detours. Instead of further loosening the global weight, I will make the early-iteration damping smoother (quadratic ramp over a longer window) so the density weight grows gradually and the placer spends more iterations in a low-congestion, wirelength-friendly regime before density pressure ramps up — this should reduce congestion-driven detours (overflow) and let the timing repair see shorter nets, lowering TNS broadly without starving density (the ramp still reaches full strength by iteration 100).

The parent relaxes the *global* density weight but the per-bin density penalty is still driven by a single scalar `density_weight`; the TNS cost comes from a few over-dense bins forcing detours. Scaling the density weight per-bin (using the preconditioner's per-region `density_weight` vector) so already-congested regions get relatively more pressure while light regions relax would reduce detours and moderate violations broadly without changing the global balance.

The parent's density relaxation is gated only on *global* overflow, but the TNS cost comes from cells being pushed into *locally* congested bins; making the HPWL-driven density relaxation conditional on the *worst-region* density (not just aggregate overflow) — i.e. relax the density weight only when both total overflow is non-increasing AND the maximum per-bin density is not growing — keeps density pressure where it is actually needed without starving wirelength globally.

The parent's density relaxation is gated only on global overflow and worst-region density, but the TNS/WNS cost comes from *timing-critical* cells being pushed into dense regions; make the early quadratic ramp of the density weight start later (longer window) and additionally keep a slightly higher floor on `mu` when HPWL is improving, so the placer spends more iterations in the wirelength-friendly regime where critical nets stay short, reducing TNS.

The parent relaxes the density weight only when *global* overflow is not rising, but the TNS cost comes from a handful of congested bins whose local overflow keeps climbing even while the global average plateaus; gate the extra density relaxation (`mu.clamp(min=0.5*LOWER_PCOF)`) on the *worst-bin* overflow trend instead of the global one, so relaxation is allowed only while no single region is getting more congested — keeping critical nets short without generating local detours that hurt TNS.

The parent relaxes the density weight only when *global* overflow is not rising, but TNS cost comes from *localized* hotspots — so gate the relaxation on the worst-region (per-bin) density instead of the global overflow, keeping full density pressure where local density is high while letting the wirelength/timing regime breathe elsewhere.

The parent gates density relaxation on global overflow, but the real TNS cost is congestion-driven detours that appear as *per-region* overflow; gate the extra relaxation (mu floor 0.5*LOWER_PCOF) on the *worst-region* overflow not having grown, so density pressure is fully restored exactly in the bins that are getting congested, while wirelength-friendly relaxation stays active where congestion is stable.

The parent's density-weight relaxations all act on the *global* density weight scalar, but the TNS cost comes from *localized* congestion where a few bins stay overfull long after the global overflow has settled; instead of touching the density weight, tighten the wirelength-model gamma schedule so that in the late stage (when overflow is already low) the HPWL model becomes more accurate (smaller gamma), which shortens critical nets without adding congestion — but clamp the gamma floor to avoid the "cells pile up" regime that hurt c014/c018.

The parent's density relaxation is a single global scalar, but the TNS cost is driven by *regional* density spikes in the hottest bins; instead of further loosening the global weight, cap the per-bin density weight growth (`density_weight_new`) more tightly in the late stage so hot regions cannot explode and displace critical cells, while leaving the global ramp untouched — this stabilizes TNS without weakening wirelength/timing pressure elsewhere.

The parent's contrastive loss already down-weights non-critical edges (via `_edge_timing_weights`), but the *area-balance repair* (`_refine_partition_by_area`) still moves whichever macro most cheaply fixes area, ignoring timing — so it can rip a timing-critical macro across tiers. Penalize moves of timing-critical macros (high incident critical-edge weight) by requiring larger area improvement before accepting them, so balance repair preserves critical-path locality.

The parent's timing-weighted contrastive loss pulls critical neighbors together, but the *area-balance repair* (`_refine_partition_by_area`) then flips whichever macro best fixes the area budget regardless of criticality, undoing those gains; make the repair prefer moving non-critical/low-degree macros by scaling each candidate's effective area with its criticality (critical macros appear "heavier", so they are less likely to be moved and, when moved, only for a larger area gain), keeping the same area target and legality.

The GNN contrastive loss uses a single global edge-weight tensor, but the *area-balance repair* then flips nodes by pure area delta, potentially undoing critical-pair co-location; by making the swap-gain prefer moving *non-critical* (low timing-weight) nodes and penalize breaking critical nets, we keep timing-critical logic co-located while still meeting area balance — reducing TNS without WNS regressions.

The parent caps *how high* the per-bin density weight can grow (4x median) but leaves the masked_scatter update free to push hot-bin weights *downward* to 1e-12 whenever `density_weight_new` is small, and — more importantly — the cap is applied to every bin uniformly, so bins that are already at the cap get no relief while the global weight keeps climbing. Instead, make the per-bin cap adaptive to the *spread* of the current per-bin weights (cap at median + k*IQR-like spread), so hot bins in a congested region are throttled relative to their peers rather than by an absolute multiple of the median, which should reduce regional detours that inflate TNS.
